short: The native Andalusian is a powerful breed built for war at the charge!
history: Compared to other armies of the period, the Muslim armies of Al-Andalus were extremely advanced and diverse; bolstered by the tenacious Berber tribes of northern Africa as well as native Andalusians and Syrian troops garrisoned across the Iberian Peninsula. The Andalusians bred war horses of their own, a renowned breed now known as "Pure Spanish", from as far back as 450BC. Despite this prodigious equine legacy, however, Umayyad cavalry lagged behind the rest of the caliphate's highly-developed military machine; the stirrup and 'framed' saddle failed to catch on, despite being used widely in its eastern territories. Conversely, Iberian Muslims used the 'curb' bit - which provided better control over the horses - centuries before anyone else.
strengths: Very low damage and armour penetration
